test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who among the following attended all the three round table conferences in London?
solution:
The correct answer is __**B.R Ambedkar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• B.R. Ambedkar and Tej Bahadur Sapru attended all three Round Table Conferences in London
 
• The participation of other leaders in the Round Table Conferences:
 
• Mahatma Gandhi and Congress: Participated in the second round table conference only
 
• Muhammad Ali Jinnah: Participated in the first and second round table conferences only

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Three Round Table Conferences were held in London between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reforms in India, especially focusing on the governance structure under British colonial rule.
 
• These conferences were convened by the British government to involve Indian political leaders and discuss the future of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• First Round Table Conference (1930–1931)
 
 
• Date: November 12, 1930 – January 19, 1931.
 
• Context: The First Round Table Conference took place amid the civil disobedience movement led by Mahatma Gandhi, particularly the Salt March (Dandi March). Gandhi was invited by the British government but did not attend this conference initially.
 
• Indian Participants: Key leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, B.R. Ambedkar, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Lala Lajpat Rai, and others attended. However, the Indian National Congress (INC) boycotted the conference, as the British had already made clear their intention not to offer complete self-rule.
 
 
 
• Second Round Table Conference (1931)
 
 
• Date: September 7 – December 1, 1931.
 
• Context: This conference was significant because Mahatma Gandhi agreed to attend after his release from prison (following the arrest during the Salt March).
 
• This marked a shift in INC’s stance.
 
• Indian Participants: Gandhi represented the INC at this conference, and other notable figures included B.R. Ambedkar, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and representatives from princely states.
 
 
 
• Third Round Table Conference (1932)
 
 
• Date: November 17, 1932 – December 24, 1932.
 
• Context: The third conference was held in the backdrop of the Poona Pact between Gandhi and Ambedkar (after Gandhi's fast in Yerwada Jail).
 
• The issue of separate electorates for Dalits was a key point of discussion.
 
• Indian Participants: B.R. Ambedkar, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and other leaders participated.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi did not attend, as he had already negotiated the Poona Pact, and the INC had little representation in this conference.
